title: Mahaveer Prasad v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Abhinava Upadhya, J.; Shamim Ahmed, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; billing dispute relegated to CGRF under clause 7.10.
headnote: On a dispute of electricity bill, the Allahabad High Court followed its order in Ram Autar (Writ-C No. 11961 of 2012, 23.10.2019) and disposed of the writ by directing the petitioners to appear before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum created under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If they approach the Forum, the application is not to be rejected only on account of delay.
facts: Mahaveer Prasad and others challenged an electricity bill of U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. On 14 May 2012 the Court stayed recovery of the impugned bill if they deposited rural-area minimum fixed charges each month, allowed meter installation, and reserved whether they would pay metered or lump-sum charges. The petition remained pending with a similar billing controversy. It was finally heard on 26 February 2020.

holding_units.topic: CGRF as forum for billing disputes
holding_units.holding: Where the controversy is a dispute of electricity bill, the writ petitioner is to appear before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum created under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if the petitioners approach the Forum, the application will not be thrown out only on account of delay.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioners are liable to pay metered charges or lump-sum fixed charges, and the merits of the impugned bill
not_decided.note: The 2012 interim order reserved the metered-versus-lump-sum question; the 2020 disposal sent the billing dispute to the CGRF without deciding either issue.
